$comment: Canonical catalog of the 7 Sorrows of Mary (Servite Rosary/Chaplet of Our Lady of Sorrows), in order. imageKey doubles as the lookup key into the merged MysteryTranslations tables (title/fruit/description per language, shipped in the bundle's mysteries maps) and the filename stem under Shared/Images/{imageKey}. Unlike the Franciscan Crown, none of the 7 reuse an existing Rosary mystery imageKey — only the Crucifixion sorrow thematically overlaps sorrowful_05_crucifixion, but is meditated distinctly here (Mary's own vantage, John 19:25–27, not Luke 23:44–46). Source of truth: Shared/content/sevenSorrows/ (devotion.json + content/<lang>.json) — no platform carries a hardcoded SevenSorrowsCatalog anymore; the whole devotion is a generic bundle. Keep in sync — see README.md in this directory.

images.note: Per-scene old masters (Rembrandt, Murillo, Veronese, Raphael, ter Brugghen, Rubens, Titian) — public domain/CC0, shipped inside the bundle; see Shared/Images/CREDITS.md.

languages.note: The 7 mystery texts ship in all six languages; the composed closing (sevenSorrowsClosingBody) is la/en only for now and falls back to the bundle's Latin elsewhere (see the bundle's validation-allowlist.json).

sorrows.title: The Loss of the Child Jesus in the Temple
Mary Meets Jesus on the Way of the Cross
sorrows.note: The one sorrow with no direct Gospel citation — a traditional devotional scene (the same status as the Stations of the Cross's 4th station), not a quoted verse.

sorrows.title: Mary at the Foot of the Cross
Mary Receives the Body of Jesus

closing.$comment: 3 Hail Marys for Our Lady's tears, then a fixed versicle/response/collect (composed into the bundle-local sevenSorrowsClosingBody key at authoring time) — unlike the Rosary/Franciscan Crown, this closing is not a user choice (no Marian-antiphon picker); it's the Servite Chaplet's own traditional close.
